questions.stem: If the $5^{\text{th}}$, $6^{\text{th}}$ and $7^{\text{th}}$ term of the binomial expansion of $(1 + x^{2})^{n+4}$ are in A.P. Then the greatest binomial coefficient in the expansion of $(1 + x^{2})^{n+4}$ is
questions.solution:
Binomial coefficient of $T_{r+1} = {}^{n+4}C_{r}$
${}^{n+4}C_{4}, {}^{n+4}C_{5}, {}^{n+4}C_{6}$ in A.P.
$\Rightarrow \frac{(n+4)!}{4!\,n!} + \frac{(n+4)!}{6!\,(n-2)!} = 2\frac{(n+4)!}{(n-1)!\,5!}$
$\Rightarrow$ Solving $n = 3$
$\Rightarrow$ Greatest binomial coefficient in the expansion of $(1 + x^{2})^{n+4} = (1 + x^{2})^{7}$
$\Rightarrow {}^{7}C_{3} = {}^{7}C_{4} \Rightarrow \frac{7!}{3!\,4!} = \frac{7 \times 6 \times 5}{6} = 35$

questions.stem: If $\vec{a} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$, $\vec{b} = 3\hat{i} + \hat{j} - \hat{k}$ and $\vec{c}$ is coplanar with $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$. Also $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{c} = 5$ and $\vec{c}$ is perpendicular to $\vec{b}$. Then $|\vec{c}|$ is
questions.solution:
$\vec{a} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$
$\vec{b} = 3\hat{i} + \hat{j} - \hat{k}$
$\vec{c}$ coplanar with $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ (Let $\vec{c} = a_{1}\hat{i} + a_{2}\hat{j} + a_{3}\hat{k}$)
$\Rightarrow (\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) \cdot \vec{c} = 0$
$(-5\hat{i} + 10\hat{j} - 5\hat{k}) \cdot (a_{1}\hat{i} + a_{2}\hat{j} + a_{3}\hat{k}) = 0$
$\Rightarrow -5a_{1} + 10a_{2} - 5a_{3} = 0$
$\Rightarrow a_{1} + a_{3} = 2a_{2}$ ...(i)
$\vec{c} \cdot \vec{b} = 0$ and $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{c} = 5$
$3a_{1} + a_{2} - a_{3} = 0$ ...(ii)
$(a_{1} + 2a_{2} + 3a_{3}) = 5$ ...(ii)
Solving (i), (ii) and (iii)
$a_{1} = \frac{1}{6},\ a_{2} = \frac{2}{3},\ a_{3} = \frac{7}{6}$
$\Rightarrow \vec{c} = \frac{1}{6}\hat{i} + \frac{2}{3}\hat{j} + \frac{7}{6}\hat{k}$
$\Rightarrow |\vec{c}| = \sqrt{\frac{11}{6}}$

questions.stem: The area of the region bounded by $S(x, y)$ such that $S = \{(x, y) : x^{2} + 4x + 2 \le y \le |x + 2|\}$ is (in sq. units)
questions.solution:
$x^{2} + 4x + 2 \le y \le |x + 2|$
(See figure: Required area $= (A_{1})$ minus $(A_{2})$, where $A_{1}$ is the region between $y = 2$ and the parabola and $A_{2}$ is the triangle.)
$A_{1} = \int_{-4}^{0} [2 - (x^{2} + 4x + 2)]dx - \frac{1}{2} \times 4 \times 2$
$= \left(\frac{-x^{3}}{3} - 2x^{2}\right)\Big|_{-4}^{0} - 4$
$= 0 - \left(\frac{64}{3} - 32\right) - 4$
$= 32 - \frac{64}{3} - 4 = \frac{20}{3}$

$\frac{dy}{dx} - \left(\frac{x}{1 + x^{2}}\right)y = \frac{\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{1 + x^{2}}}$
If $= e^{\int \frac{x}{1 + x^{2}}dx} = e^{\frac{1}{2}\ln(1 + x^{2})} = \sqrt{1 + x^{2}}$
Solution will be $y\sqrt{1 + x^{2}} = \int \frac{\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{1 + x^{2}}} \cdot \sqrt{1 + x^{2}}\,dx$
$y\sqrt{1 + x^{2}} = \frac{2x^{3/2}}{3} + c$
$y(0) = 0 \Rightarrow c = 0$
$y = \frac{2}{3}\frac{x^{3/2}}{\sqrt{1 + x^{2}}}$
Now $y(1) = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{3}$

questions.stem: If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are real numbers such that $\sec^{2}(\tan^{-1}(\alpha)) + \operatorname{cosec}^{2}(\cot^{-1}(\beta)) = 36$ and $\alpha + \beta = 8$, then $(\alpha^{2} + \beta)$ is $(\alpha < \beta)$
questions.solution:
Let $\tan^{-1}\alpha = A \Rightarrow \tan A = \alpha$
$\cot^{-1}\beta = B \Rightarrow \cot B = \beta$
$\sec^{2}A + \operatorname{cosec}^{2}B = 36$
$(1 + \tan^{2}A) + (1 + \cot^{2}B) = 36$
$\Rightarrow 1 + \alpha^{2} + 1 + \beta^{2} = 36$
$\Rightarrow \alpha^{2} + \beta^{2} = 34$
$\alpha + \beta = 8$
$(\alpha + \beta)^{2} = 34 + 2\alpha\beta = 64$
$\Rightarrow \alpha\beta = 15$
$\Rightarrow \alpha, \beta$ are roots of equation
$x^{2} - 8x + 15 = 0$
$(x - 3)(x - 5) = 0$
$\Rightarrow x = 3, 5$
$\Rightarrow \alpha = 3, \beta = 5$
$\Rightarrow \alpha^{2} + \beta = 14$

questions.stem: Two persons A and B throws a pair of dice alternatively. For A to win he should throw sum of 5 before B throws sum of 8. If A throws first, then the probability that A wins, is
questions.solution:
For sum 5, (1, 4), (2, 3) (3, 2), (4, 1) $\Rightarrow P(A) = \frac{4}{36}$
For sum 8, (2, 6), (3, 5) (4, 4), (5, 3), (6, 2) $\Rightarrow P(B) = \frac{5}{36}$
$\Rightarrow P(\bar{A}) = \frac{32}{36}, P(\bar{B}) = \frac{31}{36}$
$P(\text{A wins}) =$
$P(A) + P(\bar{A})P(\bar{B})P(A) + P(\bar{A})P(\bar{B})P(\bar{A})P(\bar{B})P(A) + \ldots$
$= \frac{P(A)}{1 - P(\bar{A})P(\bar{B})} = \frac{\frac{4}{36}}{1 - \frac{32}{36} \cdot \frac{31}{36}} = \frac{9}{19}$

questions.stem: The number of 3 digit numbers which is divisible by 2 and 3 but not divisible by 4 and 9?
questions.solution:
Total number divisible by 6
102, 108, ... 996
So total number = 150
Number divisible by 36
108, ..., 972
Total number = 25
Required number = (divisible by 6) $-$ (divisible by 36)
$= 150 - 25 = 125$

questions.stem: The product of all real roots of equation $(x^{2} - 9x + 11)^{2} - (x - 4)(x - 5) = 2$ is
questions.solution:
$(x^{2} - 9x + 11)^{2} - (x - 4)(x - 5) = 2$
$(x^{2} - 9x + 11)^{2} - (x^{2} - 9x + 20) = 2$
Let $x^{2} - 9x + 11 = t$
$t^{2} - (t + 9) = 2$
$t^{2} - t - 11 = 0$
$t = \frac{1 \pm \sqrt{1 + 44}}{2} = \frac{1 \pm \sqrt{45}}{2}$
$x^{2} - 9x + 11 = \frac{1 + \sqrt{45}}{2}$
$x^{2} - 9x = \frac{\sqrt{45} - 21}{2}$
$D_{1} : 81 - 4\left(\frac{\sqrt{45} - 21}{2}\right) > 0$
Similarly,
$x^{2} - 9x + 11 = \left(\frac{1 - \sqrt{45}}{2}\right)$
$\Rightarrow D_{2} : 81 - 4\left(\frac{-21 - \sqrt{45}}{2}\right) > 0$
$\Rightarrow$ All roots are real
$\Rightarrow$ Product of roots $= \left(\frac{\text{Constant term}}{1}\right)$
$= \left(\frac{121 - (20) - 2}{1}\right) = \frac{121 - 22}{1} = 99$

questions.stem: If $S_{n} = \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{6} + \frac{1}{12} + \ldots n$ terms. The sum of first six terms in A.P. with first term equal to $-p$ and common difference $p$ is $\sqrt{2026 \cdot S_{2025}}$. The absolute value of difference between $20^{\text{th}}$ and $15^{\text{th}}$ terms in A.P. is
questions.solution:
$S_{n} = \frac{1}{1 \cdot 2} + \frac{1}{2 \cdot 3} + \frac{1}{3 \cdot 4} + \ldots \frac{1}{n(n + 1)}$
$= \left(\frac{1}{1} - \frac{1}{2}\right) + \left(\frac{1}{2} - \frac{1}{3}\right) + \left(\frac{1}{3} - \frac{1}{4}\right) + \ldots + \left(\frac{1}{n} - \frac{1}{n + 1}\right)$
$= 1 - \frac{1}{n + 1} = \frac{n}{n + 1} \Rightarrow S_{2025} = \frac{2025}{2026}$
For A.P. $\frac{6}{2}(-2p + (6 - 1)p) = \sqrt{2026 \times \frac{2025}{2026}} = 45$
$\Rightarrow 3p = \frac{45}{3} \Rightarrow p = 5$
Now for A.P. $|a_{20} - a_{15}| = |19 \times 5 - 14 \times 5| = 25$
